proxy_language: Proto-Indo-European (late/dialectal PIE) as a deeply speculative stand-in; with Hamburgian/Ahrensburgian-era 'Old European' hydronymy as a caveat
proxy_rationale: The Bromme (c. 12,000-10,800 BCE, Allerod) and Lyngby reindeer-hunter cultures of Denmark, S Sweden and Schleswig-Holstein are known only from flint, antler and bone; their language is unrecoverable and almost certainly pre-dates any Indo-European presence in Scandinavia (which is conventionally tied to Corded Ware/Funnel Beaker c. 3000 BCE or later). No genetic or linguistic evidence links them to a known family, and the language was probably extinct without descendants (cf. 'Paleo-European' hypotheses, Vennemann's Vasconic claims are rejected by most scholars). The least misleading option for a game is a reconstructed-looking, phonotactically conservative naming system using a PIE-style root inventory with asterisk-free surface forms avoided; any name should be treated as an invented stand-in, not as attested speech. Alternative proxy of Proto-Uralic or Proto-Eskimo-Aleut-like northern foragers is equally unsupported.
phonology: Proxy (reconstructed late PIE, simplified): stops *p *t *k *kw *b *d *g *gw (with *bh *dh *gh *gwh as breathy/aspirated series, optionally collapsed to plain voiced in a simplified transliteration); fricative *s; resonants *m *n *l *r *y *w; laryngeals *h1 *h2 *h3 (optionally dropped or written h); vowels *e *o *a *i *u with length (e.g., e, o, a, i, u and long forms). Stress was pitch-accented and not marked in the orthography.
phonotactics: Roots are typically monosyllabic with shape (C)(C)eC(C) with e-grade as the basic vowel; syllable shapes CV, CVC, CCV, CVCC; word-initial clusters limited mainly to s+stop (sp-, st-, sk-) and stop+resonant (pr-, tr-, kl-, gr-, dr-, bl-); no voiced aspirate clusters mixing voiced and voiceless obstruents in a root (Bartholomae/Grassmann constraints: no two plain voiced stops, e.g. *deg- invalid; no *bhedh- in strict forms); no initial *r- (rare); words may end in vowels or -s -m -n -r -t -k. Avoid sequences like 'xu', 'kw' inside native-looking forms beyond labiovelars.
orthography: Standard PIE notation with asterisk for reconstruction in scholarly use; for game use, omit asterisk. Plain ASCII transliteration: p t k b d g, bh dh gh (or just b d g), kw, gw, s, m n l r y w, h (for any laryngeal), vowels a e i o u, optional macron or doubling for length. No c, q, x, f, z, j, v (except as w), no apostrophes needed.
morphology: Inflectional: root + thematic vowel (-e-/-o-) + ending. Nouns: stem + case/number endings; nominative singular -s (masc/fem) or zero; accusative -m; genitive -os/-es/-s; plural -es. Roots may undergo ablaut (e/o/zero). Derivational suffixes: -ti- (action noun), -tor/-ter (agent), -mo- (superlative/abstract), -ro-/-lo- (adjectival), -ent- (participle), -yo- (relational adjective), -eha2 (collective/feminine), -nt-; adjective formation by -wos/-ent.
compounding: Compounds are determinative with the modifier first and head last, joined by a thematic vowel -o- (e.g., *wlk-o- + *deh3-s style). Possessive (bahuvrihi) compounds common. 'X of Y' is rendered with a genitive suffix on Y (Y-os / Y-yo-) preceding X, or as a compound Y-o-X. Agent names via -tor suffix or compound with a verbal root as second member (e.g., X-dheh1-s 'X-placer').
noun_phrase_order: Adjective before noun (agreeing in case/number/gender); genitive before head noun; demonstratives before noun; numerals before noun.
sources: Mallory, J.P. and Adams, D.Q., Encyclopedia of Indo-European Culture, 1997
Fortson, Benjamin W., Indo-European Language and Culture: An Introduction, 2010
notes: All names for this culture are invented stand-ins. The Bromme/Lyngby language is unknown, almost certainly not Indo-European, and no real word of it survives. PIE-style forms are used only to give players internally consistent, root-based naming rather than random syllables; do not present them as the actual speech of these reindeer hunters. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word (the language is not Goidelic). Apply the audit forbidden_patterns to lowercase Latin-script names with the asterisk stripped.
